takeaway: Hot and humid Wednesday with a clearer Pacific breeze: morning partly cloudy, then isolated afternoon downpours — plan outdoors early. Surf winds: a brief morning northeasterly at Papagayo fades to light/variable today; Thursday turns west–northwest and Friday–weekend lean Pacific/onshore (choppier). Watch Tropical Wave #48 late week for a wetter pulse. Distant East Pacific storms stay near Mexico and farther west. Prolonged multi-day rain remains watch-only.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Wed–Fri)
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s weather service says falling pressure across Central America is letting the Pacific breeze show more clearly, with high humidity and earlier cloud build. Pacífico Norte today: cloudy to partly cloudy this morning, then mostly cloudy with isolated heavy afternoon showers; Nicoya heat stays sharp (around 34°C). Ensemble averages keep Nicoya daily rain mostly light to moderate — typical rainy-season cells, not a stuck rain machine — with European means a bit quieter than the U.S. average on Wednesday. The official weekly outlook still expects rains more dispersed early week, then a possible bump when Tropical Wave #48 nears later in the week. Near-surface Papagayo winds: brief northeast this morning, then light/variable; northwest tonight; west–northwest Thursday; light/variable at Papagayo with west elsewhere Friday.
periods.implications: Best outdoor window is morning before isolated afternoon storms. Expect strong heat and sticky air. For surf, any cleaner glass is mainly an early check today while a light northeasterly still exists — do not treat light/variable Papagayo as all-day offshore. Thursday softens west; Friday is a poorer wind day if west/onshore holds.
periods.confidence: High that Wednesday is a local-factor / Pacific-breeze day with isolated afternoon storms and no nearby cyclone threat. Moderate on exact Nosara shower timing and how quickly Thursday–Friday onshore verifies.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sat–Tue)
periods.pattern: Official weekly guidance still flags Tropical Wave #48 in the second half of the week as a chance to bump rain after the more scattered pattern. Longer official outlook keeps Pacífico Norte on the drier-than-normal side into early October, with weekly Pacífico Norte totals in a light-to-moderate rainy-season range (roughly 5–90 mm for the week of 28 Sep–4 Oct) and no extreme-rain event flagged. Ensemble averages show continued moist Pacific-side days around the weekend into early next week — often light to moderate daily totals near Nicoya — without a Costa Rica–centered rain machine. Marine winds trend west through Saturday, then southwest by Sunday.
periods.implications: Keep weekend plans flexible for quick storms if Wave #48 verifies. Surf-wind quality looks weaker than earlier this week: expect more Pacific/west–southwest flow and choppier faces, with only early checks for any leftover glass. Nicaragua is not showing a clean all-day offshore signal for Nosara mornings in this window.
periods.confidence: Moderate for a late-week / weekend wetter pulse tied to Wave #48 and the quieter-than-peak Pacífico Norte theme; low–moderate on exact wet-day timing and how firmly weekend onshore winds hold.

periods.label: Days 8–15
periods.pattern: Costa Rica’s longer-range outlook keeps Pacífico Norte drier than normal from late September into mid-October, with the dry signal strengthening after about October 12. No official extreme-rain event is flagged for the current week. Ensemble means still allow some moist days into early October, and the U.S. tropics outlook notes a chance of a broader Central American rain gyre pattern early in its week-2 window (around Oct 7 onward) — worth watching, not a locked-in flood spell. Distant East Pacific activity remains focused near Mexico and farther west; a new low could form south of southern Mexico late weekend / early next week and move away from Costa Rica.
periods.implications: Treat any wet day as a short cell unless a new watch develops. Outdoor and surf planning can assume the quieter Pacífico Norte lean until guidance changes; re-check midweek if a gyre signal firms up.
periods.confidence: Moderate for the quieter-than-peak theme; low for day-by-day detail and for any week-2 gyre risk past about a week.

gyreWatch.possibleTiming: No focused gyre window over Costa Rica now; residual humid instability midweek, then a general chance of a wetter pulse late week into the weekend if Tropical Wave #48 and Pacific moisture reconnect. Broader week-2 (around Oct 7+) gyre mention in U.S. tropics guidance is a longer-range watch only.
gyreWatch.supporting: Atmosphere remains humid with a clearer Pacific breeze today. Official weekly outlook cites Tropical Wave #48 later this week as a possible rain bump. Broad moist Pacific flow remains nearby offshore. Some ensemble means keep light-to-moderate Pacific-side rain into early next week. U.S. tropics outlook notes model support for a possible Central American gyre early in week-2. Distant East Pacific storms keep the far-Pacific moisture field active near Mexico.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No closed gyre sits over Costa Rica or Nicaragua on the main ensemble averages. Official Wednesday Pacífico Norte forecast is only isolated afternoon heavy showers under local / Pacific-breeze factors. Longer official outlook leans drier for northern Pacific into October, with no extreme event flagged for this week. Named East Pacific systems track along or well off Mexico, not toward Costa Rica.

surfWinds.regime: Brief NE/offshore morning Wed → light/variable → W–NW Thu → Pacific/W–SW Fri–Sun
surfWinds.detail: Papagayo waters: northeast about 10 kt this morning, then variable under 5 kt — a short offshore pulse, not a clean all-day Caribbean-trade day. Elsewhere northwest to north about 10 kt today. Tonight northwest about 10 kt. Thursday west–northwest about 10 kt, then west Thursday night. Friday light/variable at Papagayo with west about 10 kt elsewhere; Saturday similar light/variable Papagayo and west–northwest elsewhere; Sunday southwest about 10 kt. Mid-level maps are mixed early (some easterly over Nicaragua at times, more west/southwest near Nicoya on later frames) — trust the marine surface call for beach wind. Do not read Papagayo light/variable as glassy all-day offshore. Nicaragua is not offering a clear all-day offshore quality signal for Nosara this stretch.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Early this morning only while any NE/NW holds. Tonight into early Thursday may offer a brief cleaner window before west flow. Friday–Sunday favor early checks only; expect choppier Pacific/onshore–side flow. No clean all-day offshore signal this period.
surfWinds.confidence: High on the marine forecast trend (morning NE fading, then west by Thursday–Friday). Moderate on exact hour-to-hour beach winds today as Papagayo goes light/variable.

whatChanged: Yesterday’s cleaner Tue–Wed northerly/offshore call has faded: today’s Papagayo forecast is only a brief morning northeast then light/variable, with west–northwest Thursday and Pacific/west–southwest into the weekend. Official regional text now stresses a clearer Pacific breeze and earlier cloud-up. Tuesday’s storm notices aged overnight — newest avisos are Tue 29 Sep (10:30 a.m. and 5:50 p.m.) for afternoon storms under humidity and sea breezes. Polo is no longer the headline near Mexico; active East Pacific systems are Hurricane Rachel (near Mexico), Tropical Depression Nineteen-E (far west), and Tropical Storm Nolo (near Hawaii) — none threaten Costa Rica. A new area south of southern Mexico has a medium (~40%) chance of forming in 7 days. Prolonged-rain watch stays watch-only.
practical: Best outdoors: Wednesday morning before isolated afternoon storms; expect strong inland heat and sticky Pacific-breeze humidity. For surf, treat today as an early-only check — light/variable is not all-day glass — then expect softer/choppier west–southwest flow Thursday–weekend. Watch late week if Wave #48 bumps rain. Prolonged multi-day rain is not the baseline. Latest official storm notices: Tue 29 Sep (10:30 a.m. and 5:50 p.m.) — afternoon rains and thunderstorms.
